extent.title: Continuous city c. AD 100 · approximate extent
extent.note: Where building was more or less continuous around AD 100, drawn by hand at about 150 m precision from the topography of the fourteen regions (Pleiades), Platner and the general layout in Lanciani's plan, with modern atlases as reference only. It includes the gardens at the edge of the city (Pincian, Esquiline) and ribbons along the consular roads within about 700 m of it; Trastevere stops at the foot of the Janiculum. The edge is a guess: building thinned out gradually rather than stopping at a line. It is not taken from any wall; the Aurelian Walls were built in AD 271-275.

lines.title: Via Flaminia
lines.note: Built by Gaius Flaminius in 220 BC; it left the Campus Martius northwards and crossed the Tiber at the Pons Mulvius, 3 km north (Wikipedia). Drawn along today's Via Flaminia; the dashed stretch over the river is that crossing, where today's bridge (Ponte Milvio) carries another name. Where the street breaks off, the gap is drawn dashed: the road is taken to run straight on, a guess.

links.note: the Via Lata, along today's Via del Corso

lines.title: Via Salaria
lines.note: The salt road to the Sabine country, among the oldest (Wikipedia). Drawn along today's Via Salaria.

lines.title: Via Nomentana
lines.note: To Nomentum; it started at the Porta Collina of the Servian wall until the 3rd century (Wikipedia). Drawn along today's Via Nomentana.

lines.title: Via Tiburtina
lines.note: To Tibur, probably built in 307 BC (Wikipedia). Drawn along today's Via Tiburtina. Where the street breaks off, the gap is drawn dashed: the road is taken to run straight on, a guess.

lines.title: Via Labicana
lines.note: To Labici. It left the city with the Via Tiburtina at the Porta Esquilina (Pleiades, Arch of Gallienus) and passed the aqueduct crossing later called Porta Maggiore (Wikipedia). Drawn along today's Via Casilina beyond that crossing.

lines.title: Via Praenestina
lines.note: To Praeneste (Wikipedia). Drawn along today's Via Prenestina.

lines.title: Via Latina
lines.note: South-east to the Alban hills, lined with tombs (Wikipedia). Drawn along the surviving stretches named Via Latina; much of its line between is not drawn. Where the street breaks off, the gap is drawn dashed: the road is taken to run straight on, a guess.

lines.title: Via Appia
lines.note: Begun by Appius Claudius Caecus in 312 BC (Wikipedia). Outside the city the Via Appia Antica keeps the ancient line, with stretches of its paving and the tombs that lined it, so this road is marked documented; inside the later wall it follows Via di Porta San Sebastiano.

lines.title: Via Ostiensis
lines.note: To Ostia along the left bank (Wikipedia). Drawn along today's Via Ostiense.

lines.title: Via Portuensis
lines.note: To Portus, Claudius's harbour (begun AD 46), along the right bank (Wikipedia). Drawn along today's Via Portuense. Where the street breaks off, the gap is drawn dashed: the road is taken to run straight on, a guess.

lines.title: Via Aurelia
lines.note: West along the coast of Etruria, built in the middle Republic (Wikipedia). Drawn along today's Via Aurelia Antica over the Janiculum.

links.note: from the Pons Aemilius up the Janiculum

lines.title: Via Triumphalis
lines.note: From the Pons Neronianus towards Monte Mario (Pleiades), with a necropolis along it. Drawn along today's Via Trionfale, which keeps its line north of the Vatican; the link from the bridge to it is drawn by hand and is a guess. Where the street breaks off, the gap is drawn dashed: the road is taken to run straight on, a guess.

lines.title: Via Cornelia
lines.note: Ran along the north side of the Circus of Gaius and Nero (Pleiades), perhaps built by Caligula as an approach to the Horti Agrippinae (Wikipedia). No modern street keeps it: the line west from the Pons Neronianus is drawn by hand and is a guess.

lines.title: Aqua Claudia and Anio Novus · standing arches
lines.note: The arches of the Aqua Claudia that still stand in the Campagna south-east of the city, with the line of the Anio Novus beside them, as mapped in OpenStreetMap (Pleiades cites the main way). Both were begun by Caligula in AD 38 and dedicated by Claudius in 52 (Wikipedia).

lines.title: Aqua Claudia and Anio Novus · arches into the city
lines.note: From the standing arches to the city, the Anio Novus in a channel on top of the Claudia's arches, rising to over 30 m as the ground falls (Wikipedia), entering at the later Porta Maggiore. Drawn by hand through Pleiades' point for the Aqua Claudia; the line between is a guess.

lines.title: Arcus Neroniani (Claudia branch to the Caelian and Palatine)
lines.note: Nero extended the Aqua Claudia on arches from Spes Vetus on the Esquiline to the Caelian, and Domitian carried it on across the valley to the Palatine (Wikipedia). Drawn by hand from Porta Maggiore to the Palatine; the line is a guess.

zones.title: Tiber
zones.note: Today's channel (OpenStreetMap), standing in for the ancient river, which was wider and had no embankments (begun 1876). Drawn across the whole plan, inside and outside the city, simplified at 2 m; the 3D water uses the urban stretch only.

zones.title: Aniene (Anio) to its confluence with the Tiber
zones.note: Today's channel (OpenStreetMap: three river polygons from the confluence, then the Aniene relation), standing in for the ancient Anio; the confluence was controlled by Antemnae (Wikipedia). Its ancient course may have differed.

zones.title: Capitoline, Forum Romanum, Palatine, Colosseum valley and Circus Maximus
zones.note: Temples, basilicas, imperial fora (Caesar, Augustus, the Templum Pacis, Nerva's forum of AD 97), the palaces on the Palatine, the Flavian amphitheatre (AD 80) and the Circus Maximus, around Pleiades points for each. The saddle where Trajan's Forum was built from about AD 106 is outside this zone (see the Trajan's Forum zone, left out at AD 100). The outline is drawn by hand at about 100 m precision and its edges are a guess.

zones.title: Forum Boarium and Velabrum: temples, markets and the river harbour
zones.note: The cattle market by the original docks of Rome, with the temples of Portunus and Hercules Victor, the Ara Maxima, the Portus Tiberinus and the Velabrum valley up to the Forum: a place of temples, markets and trade more than of housing. The Velabrum's own edges are unclear (Wikipedia); the outline is drawn by hand at about 100 m precision and its edges are a guess.

zones.title: Oppian: Baths of Titus and the Domus Aurea pavilion
zones.note: The Baths of Titus (AD 80) and the Oppian wing of Nero's Domus Aurea, still in use by the Flavians until it burned in AD 104. The Baths of Trajan were built over it after the fire and dedicated in 109, so they are not shown at AD 100. The outline is drawn by hand at about 100 m precision and its edges are a guess.

zones.title: Caelian: Temple of the Deified Claudius
zones.note: The terrace of the Temple of Claudius, begun after AD 54 and finished under Vespasian (Wikipedia). Placed by the Regio II record; its size here is a round figure. The outline is drawn by hand at about 100 m precision and its edges are a guess.

zones.title: Forum Holitorium, Theatre of Marcellus and the Circus Flaminius porticoes
zones.note: The vegetable market and its temples, the Theatre of Marcellus (13 BC), the Porticus Octaviae and the Circus Flaminius, a public square ringed by temples and porticoes. The circus's exact line is disputed; the outline is drawn by hand at about 100 m precision and its edges are a guess.

zones.title: Central Campus Martius: Pantheon, Saepta, Baths of Agrippa and lake, Stadium of Domitian, Theatre of Pompey, porticoes up to the sundial
zones.note: Public buildings packed close: Agrippa's Pantheon and baths with their lake (Stagnum Agrippae), the Saepta Julia, the temples of the Largo Argentina, Pompey's theatre and portico, Domitian's stadium and odeum (after AD 86), and the porticoes between the Pantheon and the Horologium. Extended north to meet the Mausoleum zone; the northern edge is new and approximate. The outline is drawn by hand at about 100 m precision and its edges are a guess.

zones.title: Northern Campus Martius: Mausoleum of Augustus, Ara Pacis and the sundial
zones.note: Augustus's mausoleum and its park, the Ara Pacis (9 BC) and the Horologium, placed from their Pleiades points. The outline is drawn by hand at about 100 m precision and its edges are a guess.

zones.title: Castra Praetoria (camp of the Praetorian Guard)
zones.note: The walled camp built under Tiberius (AD 23) on the plateau beyond the Viminal. Placed as a rectangle of about 440 by 380 m; the outline is drawn by hand at about 100 m precision and its edges are a guess.

zones.title: Tiber Island: sanctuary of Aesculapius
zones.note: The island and its sanctuary (temple of Aesculapius, 291 BC; temple of Faunus, 196 BC). The island is today's outline; its ancient shore is not traced, so the edge is a guess.

zones.title: Baths of Trajan (built after the fire of AD 104, opened 109)
zones.note: Built over the Domus Aurea wing after the fire of AD 104 and dedicated in July 109 (Wikipedia), so not standing at AD 100. The outline is drawn by hand at about 100 m precision and its edges are a guess.

zones.title: Trajan's Forum and Markets (construction from c. AD 106, dedicated 112)
zones.note: The last imperial forum, cut into the saddle between the Capitoline and the Quirinal from about AD 106 and dedicated in 112, so not built at AD 100. What stood on the saddle before is uncertain; it falls to housing. The outline is drawn by hand at about 100 m precision and its edges are a guess.

zones.title: Baths of Caracalla (built c. AD 212-216)
zones.note: Built between about AD 212 and 216 (Wikipedia), so not standing at AD 100; at AD 100 the site lies in the roadside and housing zones. The enclosure is a rectangle of about 330 by 330 m round the Pleiades point. The outline is drawn by hand at about 100 m precision and its edges are a guess.

zones.title: Circus of Gaius and Nero (Vatican circus)
zones.note: Begun under Caligula (AD 37-41) and completed under Claudius, in the gardens of Agrippina, with the obelisk now in St Peter's Square on its spina (Wikipedia, Pleiades). Placed as a rectangle about 560 by 100 m round the Pleiades point, the axis east-west; the outline is drawn by hand at about 100 m precision and its edges are a guess.

zones.title: Hadrian's Mausoleum (construction from AD 134, finished 139)
zones.note: Built between AD 134 and 139 in the gardens of Domitia (Wikipedia), so not standing at AD 100. A square of about 90 m round the Pleiades point. The outline is drawn by hand at about 100 m precision and its edges are a guess.

zones.title: Vatican necropolis (tombs on the slope beside the circus)
zones.note: A burial ground on the southern slope of the Vatican hill, beside the circus and along the Via Cornelia (Wikipedia). Its extent here is a guess.

zones.title: Tombs along the Via Appia
zones.note: The Appian Way was lined with tombs outside the city; the Tomb of Caecilia Metella at the third mile (built c. 30-10 BC) is one of the best preserved (Wikipedia). Drawn along the road from the edge of the continuous city to about 400 m past that tomb, 90 m wide: the line is the road's, the width and length are a guess.

zones.title: Emporium, Porticus Aemilia and the horrea below the Aventine
zones.note: The river port on the plain south of the Aventine: the Emporium quay (Pleiades point), the Porticus Aemilia warehouse (193 BC) and the horrea (Galbana, Lolliana and others) between it and the hill. The amphora dump of Monte Testaccio was growing here; it is not modelled. The outline is drawn by hand at about 100 m precision and its edges are a guess.

zones.title: Trastevere riverfront
zones.note: A band about 100 m deep along the west bank south of the island, where landing places and storehouses for the river traffic are likely but not mapped. Its depth and extent are a guess.

zones.title: Pincian (Collis Hortorum): Horti Luculliani, Sallustiani and others
zones.note: The hill of gardens: the Horti Luculliani above the Campus and the imperial Horti Sallustiani in the valley towards the Quirinal. Mostly gardens, pavilions and a few great houses. The outline is drawn by hand at about 100 m precision and its edges are a guess.

zones.title: Esquiline: Horti Maecenatis and Lamiani
zones.note: The gardens laid out over the old Esquiline cemetery beyond the Servian agger (Maecenas's, then imperial; the Lamian gardens beside them), placed by their Pleiades points. The outline is drawn by hand at about 100 m precision and its edges are a guess.

zones.title: Esquiline and Viminal plateau
zones.note: The outer plateau between the Castra Praetoria and the aqueducts. Suburban gardens and villas are likely; nothing specific is mapped here. The extent is a guess.

zones.title: Eastern Caelian: great houses and gardens
zones.note: The eastern Caelian, towards the later Lateran, was a quarter of large houses with gardens (the house of the Laterani among them). The extent and the share of garden are guesses.

zones.title: Horti Domitiae (gardens of Domitia)
zones.note: The gardens of Domitia Longina, Domitian's wife, in the river bend where Hadrian's mausoleum was later built (Pleiades). Pleiades gives no location of its own; the outline is drawn by hand at about 100 m precision and its edges are a guess.

zones.title: Horti Agrippinae (gardens of Agrippina) on the Vatican plain
zones.note: Extensive gardens on the right bank, first owned by Agrippina the Elder and then imperial, with the circus inside them (Pleiades). Pleiades gives no location of its own; the outline is drawn by hand at about 100 m precision and its edges are a guess.

zones.title: Campus Martius by the river bend: Trigarium and Tarentum
zones.note: The open ground inside the river bend: the Trigarium exercise ground and the Tarentum, where the altar of Dis and Proserpina was used for the Secular Games (17 BC, AD 88), with the Euripus canal from Agrippa's lake. From Sulla on, insulae and villas encroached on the Campus (Wikipedia), so some building stood here too; the extent and the share left open are approximate. The outline is drawn by hand at about 100 m precision and its edges are a guess.

zones.title: Dense housing: the valleys of the east bank (Subura, Argiletum, Via Lata, the Circus Maximus side)
zones.note: Blocks of flats over shops, packed close. The Subura was "a vast and populous neighborhood" (Wikipedia) in the valley below the Esquiline, Viminal and Quirinal; the same dense fabric is attested along the Via Lata. The zone is what the others leave in the valleys, so its edges are theirs: approximate. Dated from the rebuilding after the fire of AD 64.

zones.title: Mixed housing on the hills: Quirinal, Viminal, upper Esquiline, Pincian slope
zones.note: Between the dense valleys and the gardens: temples (Quirinus, Sancus and others on the Quirinal), houses of the well-off (the Esquiline was favoured by the aristocracy for their houses) and blocks of flats. Wikipedia supports the mix but not its share or extent; the outline of the hills is drawn by hand and is a guess. Dated from the rebuilding after the fire of AD 64.

zones.title: Low-density elite housing: Aventine and Caelian
zones.note: Large houses (domus) with gardens and fewer blocks of flats. In the imperial era the Aventine became the seat of aristocratic residences, among them Trajan's own house before he became emperor; the Caelian was a fashionable residential district of the wealthy (Wikipedia). The hill outlines are drawn by hand; their edges are a guess. Dated from the rebuilding after the fire of AD 64.

zones.title: Housing: Trastevere (Regio XIV)
zones.note: Across the river: workshops, flats and immigrant communities on the flat ground below the Janiculum, generally less dense than the east-bank core. The zone is what the others leave there, so its edges are theirs: approximate. Dated from the rebuilding after the fire of AD 64.

zones.title: Roadside building along the main roads out of the city
zones.note: Shops, inns, workshops and tombs along the consular roads within about 700 m of the continuous city, narrowing from 100 m to 60 m wide with distance. The roads are sourced (see each road); the ribbons and their width are a guess. Dated from the rebuilding after the fire of AD 64.

zones.title: Suburbium · tombs, inns, workshops and small clusters along the roads
zones.note: Along each consular road from about 700 m to 2.5 km beyond the continuous city, narrowing from 60 m to 25 m wide: tombs, inns, workshops and small clusters of houses, as the tomb-lined Via Appia and Via Latina show (Wikipedia). The roads are sourced; the ribbons, their width and their length are a guess.

zones.title: Suburbium · villas, gardens and farms between the roads, thinning with distance
zones.note: Where the suburban density field is at least 0.2: it falls off with distance from the continuous city and from the roads, is zero on the rivers, and is lower on the Tiber's floodplain and on steep slopes (Mapterhorn elevation, from the modern Copernicus surface model). Villas and horti like those named on the Vatican plain and the Esquiline, farms and pasture. Nothing here is placed from a source; the field and its scales are a guess.

zones.title: Roman Campagna · farmland, pasture and scattered villas
zones.note: The low countryside round Rome beyond the suburbium (Wikipedia, Roman Campagna): farmland, pasture and scattered villas and tombs. Nothing here is placed from a source; where it begins is a guess.
zones.implicit: the frame less every other zone

markers.title: Regio I (Porta Capena)
markers.note: One of the fourteen regions into which Augustus divided the city in 7 BC. The Pleiades point lies about 1 km further south, at the later Aurelian gate; moved by hand to the Via Appia just outside Porta Capena, where the region began.

markers.title: Regio II (Caelimontium)
markers.note: One of the fourteen regions into which Augustus divided the city in 7 BC. Placed at the Pleiades representative point, derived from the places Pleiades links to the region.

markers.title: Regio V (Esquiliae)
markers.note: One of the fourteen regions into which Augustus divided the city in 7 BC. Pleiades gives this region no location; placed by hand on the Esquiline beyond the Servian agger, among the gardens the region held.

markers.title: Regio VI (Alta Semita)

markers.title: Regio XIII (Aventinus)
markers.note: One of the fourteen regions into which Augustus divided the city in 7 BC. Placed at the Pleiades representative point, derived from the places Pleiades links to the region.

markers.title: Regio XIV (Transtiberim)
markers.note: One of the fourteen regions into which Augustus divided the city in 7 BC. The Pleiades point lies across the river bend to the north-west, outside Trastevere; moved by hand to the middle of the Trastevere housing.

markers.title: Horti Lucull(i)ani
markers.note: The Pleiades point lies about 700 m north, beyond the gardens; moved by hand onto the Pincian slope above the Campus, inside the Collis Hortorum zone.

markers.title: Horti Sallustiani
markers.note: Placed at the Pleiades representative point; the zone around it is drawn from it.

markers.title: Horti Lamiani
markers.note: Placed at the Pleiades representative point; the zone around it is drawn from it.

markers.title: Emporium
markers.note: Placed at the Pleiades representative point; the zone around it is drawn from it.

markers.title: Porticus Aemilia
markers.note: Placed at the Pleiades representative point; the zone around it is drawn from it.

markers.title: Pons Neronianus
markers.note: A bridge built by Caligula or Nero to join the Campus Martius to the Vatican fields (Wikipedia); there is no direct evidence that Nero built it. Placed at the Pleiades point; the Via Triumphalis and Via Cornelia start here.

markers.title: Tomb of Caecilia Metella
markers.note: A drum on a square podium at the third mile of the Via Appia, probably built c. 30-10 BC (Wikipedia). At the Pleiades point.

markers.title: Via Triumphalis necropolis
markers.note: A stretch of imperial necropolis preserved along the road (Pleiades), at the Pleiades point.
